issues.claim: "New Jersey upgraded retail-theft crimes and directed the Attorney General ... (P.L. 2025, c.39, s.5)"
issues.problem: The rule itself is confirmed word-for-word in the enacted bill text, but the section locator appears wrong. In the njleg text the Attorney General directive and the merchant-notification route are in the numbered section that the bill's own effective-date clause calls 'section 6' (the markup renumbers it from 7 to 6.1 to 6). Section 5 in that text is the organized-retail-theft-enterprise provision. Minor citation locator error, not a misstatement of the rule.
issues.fix: Cite 's.6' (or drop the section number and cite P.L. 2025, c.39 generally). Optionally note that section 6 takes effect on the 180th day after enactment, per the act's final section.

issues.claim: fit_score legal_risk_low: 6 with a rationale listing live Section 5 exposure, defamation/false-imprisonment risk, wiretap exposure and an unclosed NJ signage gap
issues.problem: Not an error, but worth a check by the orchestrator: 6 of 15 is a mid-low score against a legal section that lists five distinct open exposures. The rationale explains the score (design removes the biometric hazard), so it is internally consistent, but the number is at the top of what the evidence supports rather than clearly low.
issues.fix: Keep 6/15, or state explicitly in the rationale that 6 assumes the review-only/no-confrontation control is contractual and enforced, and that the score would drop if staff act on unreviewed alerts.

claims_checked.claim: US retail shrink 1.6% of sales in FY2022, $112.1bn, up from 1.4% / $93.9bn in FY2021; internal + external theft ~65% of shrink; 177 brands, $1.6tn sales, 97,000+ locations
41% of retailers said no employee is authorized to stop or apprehend a shoplifter, up from 38%; 53% raised technology/software budgets and 46% increased use of third-party security personnel

Self-checkout raised loss by a mean of 22% in year one (range 3.19%-41.2%) across 8 grocery retailers / 1,300 test stores, and by +0.26 percentage points across 11 grocery retailers / 1,700 test stores, both from a set of 19 before/after studies drawn from 39 retailers with turnover >EUR 1 trillion
Missed scans are the most frequent SCO loss behaviour at 1%-4.8% of transactions, based on frequency data from 12 retailers
Retailers' estimates of the malicious share of non-scan behaviour ranged 6% to 80%
Of 14 companies testing non-scan identification, 7 reported positive findings: one 9% loss reduction, one $136m saved across 2,000 stores (0.13% sales increase), one 4.5x recovery of initial outlay
3%-10% of SCO transactions generated a non-scan nudge/alert (2 retailers, one USA one UK, plus 2 vendors) and customers self-corrected in 80%-97% of cases with a hard stop needed in 3%-20%
Regression on 4 case studies (3 retailers) puts the effect of each extra 1% of SCO transactions at 0.030%-0.048% more shrink
Middlesex County NAICS 44-45: 2,280 establishments, 37,013 employees, $45,485 average annual pay (2024)
NAICS 444140 in the county reports 13 establishments with employment withheld

FTC alleged Rite Aid generated thousands of false matches from 2012-2020 and that employees followed, searched, ordered out or called police on wrongly flagged customers, disproportionately people of colour; five-year facial-recognition ban plus notice, complaint handling, deletion, third-party assessments and CEO certification

FTC Policy Statement on Biometric Information adopted 2023 on a 3-0 vote, listing pre-collection harm assessment, surreptitious collection, vendor/end-user vetting, employee training and ongoing monitoring as unfairness factors, and warning that unsubstantiated accuracy claims may violate the FTC Act

New Jersey uprated retail-theft crimes and directs the Attorney General to 'undertake such steps as the Attorney General deems appropriate', which 'may include establishing a retail theft unit, task force, or other appropriate office or initiative', with a statutory route for a retail merchant to notify the Division of Criminal Justice of retail-theft allegations
N.J.S.A. 2C:20-11(e) shields a merchant who detains or causes arrest on probable cause from criminal or civil liability

NJ one-party consent under N.J.S.A. 2A:156A-4(d), interception under 2A:156A-3 a third-degree crime; no NJ statute requires notice or signage for ordinary workplace video cameras; N.J.S.A. 34:6B-22 covers only tracking devices in employee vehicles with penalties up to $1,000 / $2,500; 2C:14-9(d) posted notice plus lawful purpose is an affirmative defence; 2C:14-9(e)(1) fitting-room entrance carve-out but none inside a stall under (f)

NJ intrusion-upon-seclusion tort restated by the state Supreme Court in Friedman v. Martinez (2020) turns on intrusion into a private space plus conduct highly offensive to a reasonable person, tied to placement of a surveillance device rather than proof of viewing

NLRB General Counsel Memo GC 23-02 (31 Oct 2022) urges a presumptive Section 7 violation where surveillance practices viewed as a whole tend to interfere with protected activity, and would require disclosure of the technologies used, why, and how the data is used absent a business need for covert use

NJDPA (P.L. 2023, c.266) treats biometric data usable to uniquely identify a person as sensitive data but excludes photos and audio/video recordings unless generated to identify a specific individual; thresholds of 100,000 consumers (excluding data processed solely to complete a payment) or 25,000 plus revenue from selling data; 'consumer' excludes a person acting in a commercial or employment context; effective on the 365th day following enactment

Rhombus R120 mini dome $399 plus $149 licence = $548 MSRP, a $649 licence on the multisensor model, AI features and cloud archiving excluded from the Professional licence, all cameras require an ongoing licence

Ultralytics Platform plans Free $0, Pro $29/seat/month, Enterprise custom; licensing table shows AGPL 3.0 for Free and Pro and the Enterprise licence only on Enterprise; platform plans and software licences are separate

Everseen/Forrester TEI: 374% three-year ROI, payback under six months, $88,000 recovered per store per year (0.14% of covered-lane revenue), interviewed retailers $41,000-$260,000 per store, composite of 4 interviewed leaders modelled as a 200-store $20bn grocery chain; Evercheck fees charged per lane per week

NCR acquired StopLift in 2018 with deal terms not disclosed, and said it would integrate StopLift detection (checkout video compared to the POS transaction feed) into its self-checkout and store-transformation products

Solink unifies cloud video with systems such as POS for faster investigations and exception review; no published price; FAQ says installation timelines depend on location size, camera needs and whether a custom POS integration is required
Agilence integrates POS, customer, eCommerce, inventory, video and RFID data and applies machine learning to every transaction, alert and trend to rank exceptions; no price shown

Frigate: stock detectors on Coral, Hailo-8/8L, OpenVINO, ONNX/TensorRT, Rockchip and other backends; custom-model settings take a model path plus a label map; recommends 320x320 models and crops the motion region before detection
Frigate+ up to 12 fine tunes per annual subscription, $5 per additional fine tune, only a specific label set supported and no custom labels yet; subscription price not shown

Frigate+ terms restrict model use to camera systems you or your organisation own or operate and expressly prohibit deploying the models at, or operating them for, sites or systems owned or operated by your customers; commercial licences offered separately

Ultralytics ships six trackers (BoT-SORT, ByteTrack, OC-SORT, Deep OC-SORT, FastTracker, TrackTrack), TrackTrack is the default when no tracker is passed, ByteTrack is linear Kalman + IoU with no appearance model and no camera-motion compensation, BoT-SORT adds camera-motion compensation and optional ReID
Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit at $249, 8GB, 67 INT8 TOPS
Google Coral USB Accelerator starting at $59.99, out-of-stock/lead-time notice on the page
Raspberry Pi AI Kit at $70 at launch, comprising the M.2 HAT+ preassembled with a Hailo-8L, 13 TOPS

YOLOv5 + Deep SORT track-to-time-series pipeline reached 92% F1 on UCF-Crime shoplifting clips, beating RTFM by 3 points (89% baseline) and running 8.45x faster, over 544 clips (81 test clips, 14.9% abnormal) from 267 normal + 50 abnormal videos

2009 sweethearting paper uses motion-based candidate generation, spatio-temporal features, Multiple-Instance-Learning pruning and temporal-ordering validation, demonstrated on data captured in a real grocery store
LFM2-VL-450M/1.6B model card recommends fine-tuning for narrow use cases, says it is not intended for safety-critical decisions, and positions the family for low-latency edge use
Liquid AI publishes GGUF weights for a 3B LFM2-VL model with llama-mtmd-cli usage examples
Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct official weights with transformers support, vendor positioning across edge-to-cloud deployment

Cactus runs text, speech and vision models locally in one Python package with tool calling, structured extraction, transcription, image understanding and fine-tuning, and its MLX-on-Apple-silicon path exposes a local OpenAI-compatible server
